title: Capture handshake and rollback protocol for concurrent CUDA-graph captures
creator: Marco Liang
description:
Problem: Concurrent decode streams intermittently cause non-deterministic CUDA-graph capture outcomes leading to replay failures or subtle state drift during multi-stream prefill/decode. Failures manifest as: capture aborts under high occupancy, KV cache mismatches after replay, and rare kernel-binding mismatches when CUDA schedules kernels on different SMs. These issues increase tail latency and cause customer-visible correctness regressions under load.

Goal: Design and implement a lightweight handshake + rollback protocol for concurrent graph captures that: 1) makes captures idempotent and observable, 2) provides a deterministic rollback path on partial captures, 3) constrains kernel selection decisions during capture windows to guarantee replay correctness, and 4) minimizes added latency and resource contention.

Proposed approach (high level):
- Capture handshake token: each decoding stream obtains a monotonic capture token before a prefill/capture window. The token encodes epoch_id, stream_id, and sequence_number. Tokens are validated by the graph-capture coordinator to ensure non-overlapping capture regions.
- Epoch markers & window alignment: Align prefill windows to epoch boundaries. Captures may only start on epoch boundaries to avoid interleaved prefills which caused prior race conditions. Epoch boundary alignment also simplifies cache epoching for KV stores.
- Delta-capture with commit/abort semantics: Instead of committing a raw CUDA-graph immediately, we record a lightweight delta of the graph operations and kernel bindings. Only after a two-phase commit handshake (capture_success from all dependent streams) do we atomically publish the graph. If any participant reports failure or mismatch, the coordinator triggers an idempotent rollback that reverts relevant kernel reservations and frees temporary resources.
- Kernel selection constraints: During capture windows, kernel selection uses a restricted candidate set determined by (sequence_length, batch_cohort, model_variant). This avoids late-binding kernel changes across capture vs replay. A fallback path allows broader kernel selection at the expense of starting a fresh capture.
- Attention fusion gating: Gate attention-fusion optimizations during capture if sequence length or occupancy could change between capture and replay. Use a learned heuristic (from metric profiles) to decide when fusion is safe.
- Shadow capture & verification: Run shadow captures in a low-overhead path for a subset of requests (shadow_rate adjustable) to verify that captured graphs replay deterministically. Shadow results are compared asynchronously to production outputs for regression detection.
- Test harness & fuzzing: Expand our existing multi-stream harness to perform stress fuzzing across kernel candidate sets, variable sequence lengths, and preemption scenarios. Capture failure rate targets and regression detectors are integrated into the harness.

Why this is different from previous efforts: Prior tickets focused on improving capture determinism via kernel-probing and segmentation heuristics. This task introduces a coordination protocol across streams (handshake + epoching + two-phase commit) and explicit rollback paths, plus an operationally-safe shadow verification pipeline to catch regressions before rollout.

Success criteria: see acceptance_criteria below.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end handshake implemented: streams acquire and validate capture tokens before starting capture windows
Two-phase commit implemented: captured graphs are atomically published only after all participants acknowledge success
Rollback path verified: partial/failed captures reliably revert resource reservations without leaving dangling kernel bindings
Kernel-selection constraints enforced during capture windows with documented heuristic thresholds
Shadow capture verification shows deterministic replay for 99.99% of shadowed requests across a 24h stress run
Capture failure rate reduced to <0.01% under synthetic 95th-percentile load compared to baseline
No customer-facing regressions in canary (0.5% traffic) for 72 hours
Monitoring dashboards added: capture_attempts, capture_commits, capture_aborts, shadow_mismatch_rate, replay_kv_mismatch
work_notes: 2026-03-02: Design sync. Attendees: Aisha, Marco, Elena (infra), Sam (runtime). Agreed on capture token shape and epoch alignment. Action: Aisha to prototype coordinator state machine.
2026-03-04: Prototype implemented (coordination FSM + token validation) in branch: github.com/redwood-inc/runtime/PR-1423. Initial unit tests for token sequencing passing.

2026-03-05: Observed that under high burst load, coordinator state queue increased commit latency by ~1.8ms. Trade-off: batching commit acknowledgements vs per-capture atomicity. Decided to keep per-capture commit for correctness; optimize later via commit coalescing.
2026-03-06: Kernel selection constraint API sketched: KernelPolicy{sequence_threshold, occupancy_bucket, allow_fusion}. Elena to implement enforcement hooks in kernel selector.
2026-03-07: Implemented delta-capture recorder. It records kernel binding list + memory reservation diffs. Stored ephemeral in /var/tmp/graph_deltas until commit/abort.

2026-03-08: First end-to-end smoke test: 10k concurrent prefill cycles. Results: 12 capture aborts due to transient allocation conflicts. Rollback path successfully released reservations in all cases. Root cause: allocator fragmentation; follow-up task created (ENG-210112).

2026-03-09: Shadow capture pipeline integrated with telemetry. Initial shadow_rate set to 0.1%. One mismatch detected — investigation shows an attention kernel returning different floats at extremal sequence lengths due to a rounding codepath. Filed follow-up with kernel team (ENG-210221).
2026-03-10: Code submitted for review: PR-1439 (coordinator + delta commit), PR-1440 (kernel-policy hooks), PR-1441 (shadow verification). Requested review from Sam (runtime) and Priya (QA).
rollout_plan: Stage 0 - unit/integration tests + fuzz harness: run in CI for all PRs (required)
Stage 1 - internal cluster shadow-only (shadow_rate=1%): validate for 48 hours
Stage 2 - canary: route 0.5% production traffic with full commit semantics for 72 hours
Stage 3 - ramp to 10% if no regressions, continue monitoring for 7 days
Stage 4 - global rollout with opt-in for legacy kernel policy for 2 weeks before full switch
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Coordinator becomes a bottleneck under extreme parallelism. Mitigation: implement sharded coordinators keyed by GPU-device and batch-cohort, and add commit coalescing optimization.
Risk: Added handshake latency increases tail token latency. Mitigation: micro-benchmark handshake path and optimize using lock-free queues; set p95 target of <1ms added overhead.
Risk: Kernel-policy over-constraining hurts throughput. Mitigation: allow config toggles per deployment and collect policy effectiveness telemetry to relax constraints safely.
Risk: Shadow mismatch noise causes alert fatigue. Mitigation: adaptive thresholding and automated triage that suppresses alerts for known benign numerical diffs under epsilon bounds.
qa_plan: Expand fuzz harness to cover: preempted captures, stream restarts, allocator OOM, kernel-binding permutations
Add deterministic CI job that runs 1M synthetic prefill/replay cycles nightly for the branch
Manual QA: targeted regression tests for attention kernels at boundary sequence lengths
Load test: 24h run with production traffic profile on staging cluster with shadow_rate=5%
review_feedback: Sam (runtime): 'Coordinator design looks sound; please ensure the commit log is compact and avoid long-lived disk persistence for deltas.'
Priya (QA): 'Need stronger QA targets for shadow mismatch tolerances; add automatic rollback on any mismatch during canary.'
Elena (infra): 'Sharding coordinator by GPU device is required for scale; document sharding keys and failure modes.'
